theory.intro: A quadrilateral is **convex** when all four of its interior angles are less than $180^{\circ}$. If one interior angle is reflex — bigger than $180^{\circ}$ — the quadrilateral is **non-convex** (also called concave) and has a dent in its outline.
facts: **Convex**: every interior angle is less than $180^{\circ}$.
**Non-convex**: at least one interior angle is reflex, so a vertex points back into the shape.
Diagonal test: in a convex quadrilateral both diagonals lie inside the shape and meet inside it.
In a non-convex quadrilateral one diagonal lies outside the shape, so the two diagonals do not cross inside it.
A square, a rectangle, a rhombus and a parallelogram are all convex.
steps: Look around the outline for a vertex that points back into the shape — a dent.
Check the interior angle at that vertex: is it more than $180^{\circ}$?
One reflex interior angle makes it non-convex; if every interior angle is less than $180^{\circ}$ it is convex.

practice.coverageNote: Single yes/no recognition atom: the only in-skill depth is combining the reflex-angle test with the diagonal test, which supports two mastery cards without repeating the same judgement.

foundation.solution_text:
Every vertex points outwards, so no interior angle is reflex.
Convex

The angle at the lower-right vertex is close to a straight angle, but it is still less than $180^{\circ}$, and so is every other angle.
Convex

The outline turns inwards at the middle vertex, giving a reflex interior angle there.
Non-convex

foundation.question_text: The four interior angles of a quadrilateral are $105^{\circ}$, $80^{\circ}$, $95^{\circ}$ and $80^{\circ}$. Is it convex or non-convex?
foundation.solution_text:
The largest angle is $105^{\circ}$, which is less than $180^{\circ}$, so no angle is reflex.
Convex

foundation.question_text: The four interior angles of a quadrilateral are $40^{\circ}$, $215^{\circ}$, $60^{\circ}$ and $45^{\circ}$. Is it convex or non-convex?
foundation.solution_text:
$215^{\circ}$ is bigger than $180^{\circ}$, so that angle is reflex.
Non-convex

foundation.question_text: Is a rectangle convex or non-convex? Explain your answer.
foundation.solution_text:
Every interior angle of a rectangle is $90^{\circ}$.
$90^{\circ}$ is less than $180^{\circ}$, so no angle is reflex.
Convex

development.solution_text:
Each dashed diagonal stays inside the outline, and the two diagonals cross inside the shape.
Convex, because the diagonals meet inside the quadrilateral.

One diagonal runs outside the outline, and the two diagonals only meet once one of them is followed outside the shape.
Non-convex, because one of the diagonals lies outside the quadrilateral.

The shape is long and thin, but the outline still turns back on itself at the middle vertex.
The interior angle there is bigger than $180^{\circ}$.
Non-convex

development.question_text: The four interior angles of a quadrilateral are $30^{\circ}$, $255^{\circ}$, $40^{\circ}$ and $35^{\circ}$. Is it convex or non-convex?
development.solution_text:
Three of the angles are small, but $255^{\circ}$ is bigger than $180^{\circ}$.
One reflex interior angle is enough.
Non-convex

At $E$, $F$ and $H$ the outline turns outwards, so those interior angles are less than $180^{\circ}$.
At $G$ the outline turns back into the shape, so the interior angle opens past a straight angle.
The interior angle at $G$ is reflex.

development.question_text: Explain why a square, a rectangle and a parallelogram are all convex.
development.solution_text:
Every angle of a square and of a rectangle is $90^{\circ}$.
The angles of a parallelogram come in two equal pairs, and each of them is less than $180^{\circ}$.
None of these shapes has a reflex interior angle, so all three are convex.

mastery.question_text: Both diagonals of quadrilateral $WXYZ$ lie inside the shape. What does this tell you about the interior angles of $WXYZ$?
mastery.solution_text:
A diagonal only leaves the shape when a vertex points back inwards.
Both diagonals staying inside means no vertex points inwards.
Every interior angle of $WXYZ$ is less than $180^{\circ}$, so $WXYZ$ is convex.

The diagonal Ravi drew, $BD$, does lie inside the shape, but one diagonal inside is not the test.
The other diagonal, $AC$, runs above $D$ and lies outside the shape.
The interior angle at $D$ is reflex, so $ABCD$ is non-convex.
